policy: Only executed behavior tests justify passing-baseline. Symbol/name availability in the API inventory is not behavioral compatibility. Pending rows are fixture scaffolding, not passing tests or xfails; add evidence as restoration tasks are implemented.

Writer verified; standalone public SQL reader is recorded separately and Model-derived empty types are recorded separately under schema-correct-parquet-sql. Timezone-aware nanosecond schemas, including nested fields, are rejected before DuckDB single-file merging or schema-promotion reads to prevent precision loss. Task 2.4 additionally verifies literal wildcard characters in scratch directory paths for both partitioned and single-file output, including schema-promotion metadata/data reads and DuckDB merging.

Standalone query_parquet reads files, numbered managed parts in numeric order, or recursive ordinary datasets through a connection-local DuckDB results view and Arrow into Polars. Verified exact strings, Int64, nulls, Decimal(20,4), naive microsecond/nanosecond datetime, column order, SQL filtering/grouping/aggregation, positional/named parameters, literal glob characters, lazy imports, database forwarding, preservation of existing results tables/views on success or SQL failure, detached results, and cleanup on errors and KeyboardInterrupt. Supported timezone-aware timestamps normalize to UTC with microsecond precision; nanosecond timezone-aware schemas, including nested fields, fail metadata preflight to prevent DuckDB precision loss. Original timezone metadata is not preserved. Model-derived schema restoration and Query/CSV integration are recorded separately under schema-correct-parquet-sql and csv-input-options-and-ownership. Task 2.4 additionally verifies metadata preflight uses literal paths without buffering file contents and rejects external Int128 annotations, including nested fields, before DuckDB reads them as binary.

Standalone lazy import_csv accepts a local literal Path/string or borrowed readable text/binary stream, scans directly into one staged Parquet file, and atomically publishes only after success. Verified explicit String identifiers with leading zeros, Unicode/quoted commas/newlines, exact Int64/Decimal/microsecond and naive nanosecond datetime values, nulls, separator/header/quote/encoding/new-column options, preservation of caller option containers, empty typed/header-only schemas, validation without network, collisions including hard links and borrowed files, and cleanup/old-output restoration on malformed or late parse errors, sink errors, and KeyboardInterrupt before and after publication rename. Int128 schema overrides normalize to Decimal(38,0); overflow, columnless empty input, and nanosecond timezone schemas fail without publication. File inputs use lazy scan/sink without full DataFrame collection or temporary CSV files. Polars buffers borrowed stream contents; nonseekable sources use an owned in-memory adapter. Borrowed streams stay open but cursor position is not preserved. Publication provides exception safety, not crash durability or concurrent-writer coordination. Query/fetch CSV integration remains pending task 2.5 and list CSV integration tasks 6.1 and 6.2. Nonempty full schema defaults raise_if_empty to False for typed zero-row empty input while preserving explicit raise_if_empty=True; partial schema_overrides retain Polars defaults.

Executed offline public logic-node, parser, dynamic default, validation, immutable serialized spec logic, XML/executor, and independent clone contracts. Historical strings bind OR before AND and complete the preceding operation at a closing group. deviations: Nested opening markers are retained when inner groups close. This intentionally changes previously successful upstream grouping: B OR ((A OR C) AND D) now means B or ((A or C) and D), whereas pinned upstream produced (B or A or C) and D. With B true and D false the repaired result is true and upstream's result was false. Historical OR-before-AND and preceding-operation completion at a closing group remain.
Malformed expressions raise parser errors instead of upstream internal stack/assert failures; compact operator aliases and multi-letter codes are supported.
SortOrderList.next retains the existing native repair returning the first element without consuming it; upstream next(list) raises TypeError.

Verified string IDs, exact large integers, Unicode/newlines, Decimal/Date/nulls, selected empty headers, CSV parsing and pagination controls, compression as a Parquet intermediate control, resource free-space preflight, literal quote/glob paths, expanded return paths, source/hard-link/borrowed collisions including managed partition parts, and cleanup with old-output rollback on producer/COPY errors and interrupts before or after publication. Shared managed-part collision validation also protects path and borrowed CSV sources through direct to_parquet and to_duckdb calls. Format/suffix conflicts reject before producer/output creation. Model-derived empty types are recorded separately under schema-correct-parquet-sql. Publication provides exception safety, not crash durability or concurrent-writer coordination.
